project_name: Drug Solubility Prediction using Machine Learning
objective: Predict aqueous solubility of drug molecules using Morgan fingerprints + RDKit descriptors and XGBoost

methodology.feature_extraction: Morgan Fingerprints (radius=2, nbits=2048) + 7 RDKit physicochemical descriptors (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings)
methodology.feature_selection: SelectFromModel (Random Forest importance, threshold=median), fit on the training fold only
methodology.hyperparameter_tuning: GridSearchCV (5-fold CV) per model, inside a single Pipeline(scaler, selector, model) to avoid leakage - see SPEC.md

external_validation.dataset: AqSolDB (Sorkun et al. 2019), deduplicated against ESOL by canonical SMILES

key_insights: Adding physicochemical descriptors alongside the fingerprint was the single biggest lever: MolLogP alone accounts for 17.5% of feature importance, more than the next 5 fingerprint bits combined - consistent with LogP's well-known role in aqueous solubility (Yalkowsky's General Solubility Equation)
Test R² = 0.9116 vs the fingerprint-only Random Forest baseline's 0.6985 - a substantial improvement, not just noise, given the train/test gap also shrank (0.064 vs the baseline's 0.24)
XGBoost outperformed Random Forest, Gradient Boosting and SVR on 5-fold CV

Honest external check: R² drops to 0.638 on 8,881 AqSolDB compounds never seen during training (after removing the 1,099 that overlap with ESOL) - the in-distribution 0.91 does not fully transfer, which is the expected and correctly-measured pattern, not a red flag
Feature selection (SelectFromModel, fit on the training fold only) kept 1,028 of 2,055 features
